title: The Flood Shortcut Stays Off the Map
premise: A traveler wants a route through a fictional town during a flood warning, but a navigation line does not reflect the warning. A reviewed safety message pauses the trip and directs decisions to current official closures and instructions.
hook: Does a line on the map know what the water is doing?
visible_action: A route line meets a flood-warning overlay and stops; official closure information becomes a required decision input.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Navigation suggestions do not replace current hazard warnings and official instructions.
gate: Use current authoritative flood-safety guidance; never show water-entry thresholds, crossing tests, or improvised escape actions. Do not ask viewers to guess an emergency response or choose an action in a simulated emergency; any response content must come from reviewed official guidance.

editorial_pick.original_reason: A calm preparedness episode fits the survival/learning direction and avoids turning danger into a guessing game.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: After source approval, use a clearly labeled map illustration to explain why the proposed flood shortcut is removed.
editorial_pick.gate: Hold production until current authoritative flood-safety guidance is checked for the intended region. Do not stage a traversable flood-depth challenge.
editorial_pick.note: These are the catalogue's historical editorial recommendations, not current owner-approved selections or guaranteed watchable stories. Reapply the latest comedy/suspense gate.
